Elena / Hannah — I reviewed the v3 redline and have inline legal edits. Summary up front: we should avoid open-ended timing for credits, define the surcharge corridor numerically, and add a short operational playbook for >3x events. Below are the proposed redline points (I will attach a tracked-changes doc):

- Footnote 4: replace with: "Surcharge Credit Mechanics: Any surcharge amount identified in month M that falls within the Surcharge Corridor (as defined in Section 2.1) shall be credited as a flow-through on invoice for month M+1. Surcharge amounts that exceed the Corridor threshold for more than one (1) month in any rolling ninety (90) day period shall be subject to reconciliation on a quarterly basis and may be applied against the next quarter's invoice with prior notice to the Customer."

- Escrow / Security: For reconciliation amounts > $Y (we should agree a dollar threshold relative to forecast; propose $100k or 10% of monthly committed spend, whichever is greater) the Parties will place the disputed amount in an interest-bearing escrow pending reconciliation. 

- Extreme Variance ( >3x forecast): add operational steps: (i) immediate notification window (24 hours), (ii) provisioning pause option for Redwood with a 5-business-day cure period to allow capacity scaling or manual rate-limiting, (iii) if unresolved, temporary application of a pre-agreed provisional surcharge at 150% of the regular surcharge to account for expedited capacity.

- Numeric examples: include a worked example in Annex A to show how flow-through vs. quarterly true-up would appear on invoices. This usually helps procurement buy-in.

I attached a tracked-changes Word that applies the above. I'm deliberately leaving the exact $Y escrow threshold blank for commercial negotiation — Hannah / Laura, please propose the commercial bucket you think is reasonable and I'll bake it into the language.
